cases.question_text: How many emails were exchanged between Kenneth Lay and Leonardo Pacheco?
cases.normalized_question: How many emails were exchanged between Kenneth Lay and Leonardo Pacheco?
cases.reference_answer: In the current local export, 23 emails were exchanged between Leonardo Pacheco and Kenneth Lay, and the traffic is one-way: the messages run from Leonardo Pacheco to Kenneth Lay. The content is EnronOnline executive-summary reporting rather than back-and-forth discussion.
cases.canonical_sql:
SELECT
  'leonardo.pacheco@enron.com' AS entity_a,
  'kenneth.lay@enron.com' AS entity_b,
  SUM(CASE
        WHEN LOWER(person_a) = 'leonardo.pacheco@enron.com'
         AND LOWER(person_b) = 'kenneth.lay@enron.com'
        THEN total_count ELSE 0 END) AS sent_a_to_b,
  SUM(CASE
        WHEN LOWER(person_a) = 'kenneth.lay@enron.com'
         AND LOWER(person_b) = 'leonardo.pacheco@enron.com'
        THEN total_count ELSE 0 END) AS sent_b_to_a,
  SUM(total_count) AS total_emails
FROM communication_dyads
WHERE (LOWER(person_a) = 'leonardo.pacheco@enron.com'
   AND LOWER(person_b) = 'kenneth.lay@enron.com')
   OR (LOWER(person_a) = 'kenneth.lay@enron.com'
   AND LOWER(person_b) = 'leonardo.pacheco@enron.com')
required_instructions: Honor directionality and avoid saying 'exchanged' when all traffic is one-way.
Use communication_dyads as the benchmark reference for pair totals.

cases.canonical_sql:
SELECT
  contact_email,
  SUM(sent_to_contact) AS sent_to_contact,
  SUM(received_from_contact) AS received_from_contact,
  SUM(total_emails) AS total_emails
FROM (
  SELECT
    d.person_b AS contact_email,
    SUM(d.total_count) AS sent_to_contact,
    0 AS received_from_contact,
    SUM(d.total_count) AS total_emails
  FROM communication_dyads d
  WHERE LOWER(d.person_a) = 'kenneth.lay@enron.com'
  GROUP BY d.person_b

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    d.person_a AS contact_email,
    0 AS sent_to_contact,
    SUM(d.total_count) AS received_from_contact,
    SUM(d.total_count) AS total_emails
  FROM communication_dyads d
  WHERE LOWER(d.person_b) = 'kenneth.lay@enron.com'
  GROUP BY d.person_a
) combined
GROUP BY contact_email
ORDER BY total_emails DESC, contact_email ASC
LIMIT 1
required_instructions: Rank by total_emails and preserve inbound/outbound directionality in the answer.
Treat this as a ranking query over communication_dyads rather than evidence search.

cases.canonical_sql:
WITH weekly_counts AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(period AS DATE) AS period,
    total_count,
    to_count,
    cc_count,
    bcc_count
  FROM communication_dyads
  WHERE LOWER(person_a) = 'leonardo.pacheco@enron.com'
    AND LOWER(person_b) = 'kenneth.lay@enron.com'
    AND CAST(period AS DATE) IN (DATE '2000-12-04', DATE '2000-12-11')
),
comparison AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN period = DATE '2000-12-04' THEN total_count END) AS start_count,
    MAX(CASE WHEN period = DATE '2000-12-11' THEN total_count END) AS end_count
  FROM weekly_counts
)
SELECT
  weekly_counts.period,
  weekly_counts.total_count,
  weekly_counts.to_count,
  weekly_counts.cc_count,
  weekly_counts.bcc_count,
  comparison.end_count - comparison.start_count AS delta_total_count
FROM weekly_counts
CROSS JOIN comparison
ORDER BY weekly_counts.period
required_instructions: Return both weekly rows and the delta between them.
Keep the comparison on the same dyad and the same local export snapshot.

adr_log.title: Keep governed question bank as the single evaluation SSOT
adr_log.context: The repo already centralizes question curation and governed exports in src/evaluation/question_bank.py.
options_considered: Create a separate Genie-only benchmark store
Extend the governed question bank with Genie benchmark metadata
adr_log.decision: Extend the governed question bank and freeze a derived Genie benchmark subset from it.
adr_log.rationale: Avoids dataset drift and preserves one promotion path across regression, AVL, benchmark, and holdout layers.
trade_offs: Some benchmark-specific fields live outside the core bank as derived artifacts
risks: Snapshot drift between reference answers and current local exports
mitigations: Keep the benchmark as a generated derivative
Track question-bank vs snapshot alignment explicitly
rollback_conditions: The governed bank cannot express benchmark metadata without repeated manual duplication
adr_log.superseding_evidence_trigger: Repeated evidence that a separate benchmark registry is materially simpler without introducing drift.

adr_log.title: Migrate only the analytics_sql_genie slice first
adr_log.context: Genie is strongest for benchmarkable analytical SQL and weakest for graph, evidence, and vector-heavy flows.
options_considered: Broad Genie migration across graph and evidence tools
adr_log.decision: Advance the governed quantitative slice first, then require benchmark evidence before expanding.
adr_log.rationale: This is the smallest valuable, reversible migration boundary already represented in the question bank.
trade_offs: Some analytics remain on DuckDB/Lakebase while Genie matures
risks: Benchmark vanity wins without broader trust improvements
rollback_conditions: Quantitative slice fails to improve or preserve trust metrics
adr_log.superseding_evidence_trigger: A shadow benchmark shows another tool family clearly outperforms the quantitative slice as the first migration target.

adr_log.title: Use hybrid wrappers for entity-resolved analytics
adr_log.context: Several analytical tools are SQL-native but depend on entity resolution, directional semantics, and evidence packaging.
options_considered: Keep the full path on DuckDB/Lakebase
Use a hybrid wrapper with local resolution and governed SQL execution
adr_log.decision: Keep entity resolution and evidence packaging outside Genie while letting Genie or Databricks SQL handle the analytical core.
adr_log.rationale: Separates deterministic correctness work from SQL natural-language generation.
trade_offs: Wrapper behavior must stay stable across backends
mitigations: Exact benchmark rows with failure-mode tags
rollback_conditions: Wrapper complexity grows without measurable benchmark lift
adr_log.superseding_evidence_trigger: Genie reliably absorbs entity resolution without regressions on benchmark or adversarial slices.

adr_log.title: Preserve DuckDB as local-fast reference and Lakebase as governed remote reference
adr_log.context: The project already depends on local-fast iteration and governed production-style SQL access.
options_considered: DuckDB and Lakebase as reference layers
adr_log.decision: Use local DuckDB for benchmark authoring and Lakebase/Databricks SQL for governed parity and remote validation.
adr_log.rationale: Maintains fast iteration while keeping production-style SQL as a stable reference.
mitigations: Pinned envs for every benchmark run
adr_log.superseding_evidence_trigger: A unified local semantic-layer emulator proves reliable enough to replace the current dual-reference model.

adr_log.title: Keep graph, vector, evidence, and provenance tools off Genie until evidence says otherwise
adr_log.context: Current graph, evidence, and provenance tools are specialized and governed by deterministic retrieval quality.
options_considered: Expand Genie into graph and evidence lanes now
adr_log.decision: Keep those lanes on DuckDB/Lakebase or their specialized backends until a dedicated pilot proves a win.
adr_log.rationale: Protects graph semantics and evidence-grounding quality.
trade_offs: The target state is intentionally not fully uniform
rollback_conditions: Not applicable until a dedicated pilot exists
adr_log.superseding_evidence_trigger: A controlled shadow benchmark shows a clear gain with zero trust loss.

adr_log.title: Certify every migration with layered evaluation and holdout gates
adr_log.context: The repo already has regression, adversarial, SQL-first, and improvement-loop assets.
options_considered: Layered gating across regression, adversarial, Genie benchmark, and holdout
adr_log.decision: Use all four evaluation layers for promotion, pause, and rollback decisions.
adr_log.rationale: Prevents benchmark overfitting and protects non-Genie behavior.
mitigations: Start with a small governed Genie subset
rollback_conditions: Holdout or AVL turns red while benchmark stays green

adr_log.title: Normalize backend defaults before comparing architectures
adr_log.context: Runtime config defaults to local while agent_serving defaults to lakebase.
adr_log.decision: Record the mismatch in the SSOT manifest and pin benchmark environments explicitly in every run.
adr_log.rationale: Avoids false wins or losses caused by implicit backend selection.
risks: Silent drift if env pinning is skipped
mitigations: Make env pinning part of the baseline artifact
rollback_conditions: Not applicable until defaults are unified in code
adr_log.superseding_evidence_trigger: The backend defaults are unified across runtime and agent surfaces.

gating_policy.expand: green on benchmark, regression, AVL, and holdout layers
gating_policy.pause: plateau below 2pp over two iterations or maintainability worsens
gating_policy.rollback: any red trust metric, >2pp canonical regression, >5% hard-failure rate, or >20% latency regression without compensating gains

metrics.red: any trust regression or evidence fabrication

metrics.name: latency
metrics.target: p95 not worse than baseline for pure Genie and not worse than +10-15% for hybrid

metrics.name: failure_rate
metrics.measurement_method: failed or empty responses divided by total benchmark questions

metrics.name: cost
metrics.measurement_method: token and SQL execution cost per question
metrics.data_source: MLflow traces and Databricks query metrics

metrics.name: maintainability
metrics.target: 20% reduction in duplicate analytics logic and smaller change surface
metrics.measurement_method: code inventory and files touched per analytics change

metrics.name: developer_effort
metrics.target: 25% reduction in median time to passing validation

metrics.name: governance_trust_fit
metrics.target: no regression and zero policy leaks
metrics.measurement_method: weighted trust composite over grounding, citation, provenance, and access control
metrics.data_source: enron evaluation, bible governance, and ABAC slices
metrics.green: flat or better with zero critical violations
metrics.red: any policy leak or trust regression >1pp

metrics.name: adversarial_robustness
metrics.target: +5pp on escalated slices and zero critical fabrication failures
metrics.measurement_method: adversarial scorer means and critical fail counts
metrics.red: any critical fail or no improvement over two iterations
